newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's UES to limit power to debtor regions.
newsitem.headline: Russia's UES to limit power to debtor regions.

text.p: Russia's national power utility Unified Energy System (UES) will limit electricity supplies to some regions which have not paid their bills from August 8, Interfax news agency said on Thursday.

It quoted UES Central Dispatch Unit Head Alexander Bondarenko as saying UES would restrict power supplies to the Bryansk and Belgorod regions and to Mordovia, Kalmykiya and Kabardino-Balkariya republics.
UES had cut power to some regions by 25-30 percent from July 20, Interfax said.
The cuts appeared to be a new weapon in the electricity monopoly's arsenal to combat non-payment which is endemic in the Russian energy sector.
Together the regions and republics facing cuts owe a total of 1.42 trillion roubles ($245 billion), Bondarenko said, adding UES had such limits in place for the Lipetsk and Arkhangelsk regions.
Kurgan and Pskov regions paid their bills after limits were imposed and have had sanctions lifted, he said.

Russia has limited UES's ability to cut off non-payers but in recent months Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov and UES officials, many appointed at the demand of the state which holds a controlling stake in UES, have begun new energy payment plans.
Major industrial customers are promised direct access to the wholesale electricity market, the system from which supplies to Bryansk and other regions will be limited.
Regions near Moscow are also taking part in a plan to cut prices for customers who pay cash and in advance.
